crate.rule: The Cargo package, library and binary name is always som_app. The prompt package name appears only in README.md. So Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are the same bytes for every product.

files.rule: Reads DATABASE_URL, which is required, and SOM_APP_ADDR, which defaults to 127.0.0.1:8000. Connects a PgPool, runs som_app::MIGRATOR, then serves som_app::router(pool). A missing DATABASE_URL prints one line to stderr and exits with status 2.
Declares the modules api, db, models and schemas. Exports pub fn router(pool: sqlx::PgPool) -> axum::Router from api, and pub static MIGRATOR: sqlx::migrate::Migrator = sqlx::migrate!().
Row structs that derive sqlx::FromRow. v1 to v4 use Row. v5 uses ParentRow and ChildRow.

Request and response structs that derive serde traits. v1 to v4 use Create, Update and Read. v5 uses ParentCreate, ParentUpdate, ParentRead, ChildCreate, ChildUpdate, ChildRead and ParentWithChildrenCreate. ParentWithChildrenCreate has exactly the members parent (a ParentCreate) and children (1 to 20 ChildCreate values), and the batch response has exactly the members parent (a ParentRead) and children (ChildRead values in the same order as the Python product), as in contracts/related-business.v1.md. Prompt field names never become members of these two wrapper objects, so a field named parent or children does not collide. Struct members named by a prompt field keep the field name on the wire, with serde rename where the Rust member is a raw identifier, and sqlx row mapping uses the same column name. Request structs reject unknown members only where the Python product does (v3 to v5).
axum handlers, the router, the /healthz route, the JSON fallback for 404 and 405, and the mapping of every extractor rejection to the frozen 422 body.
Every SQL statement, as a string constant with double-quoted identifiers, and the functions that run them with the sqlx runtime API.

The schema for the prompt. <revision> is migration.revision verbatim. The first line is the comment -- revision: <revision>, down_revision: <down_revision or none>. sqlx needs the integer version prefix 0001.

Product tests. They read TEST_DATABASE_URL. A missing variable fails the test; it is never a skip. Each test drops and recreates schema public, runs MIGRATOR, and drives som_app::router with tower::ServiceExt::oneshot.
Names the prompt package, the prompt version, the routes, and the run, test and migration commands from toolchain.json.

naming.rust_items: Type, module, function and crate names come from a fixed table by role. No Rust item name comes from the prompt.
naming.fields: A struct field uses the prompt field name. A Rust keyword that can be raw is written r#name. serde and sqlx see the plain name, so JSON members and columns use the field name verbatim.
naming.sql: Table, column and constraint identifiers are double-quoted verbatim prompt names. Values are always bound parameters. No prompt text is pasted into SQL except quoted identifiers.
naming.unique_constraints: Names are not compared. A unique field gets a UNIQUE constraint. The foreign key gets REFERENCES parent(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT.
naming.indexes: The migration creates the same indexes as the Python migration for the same prompt: the same tables, columns in the same order, and the same uniqueness. Index names are not compared.

types.id: i32 in Rust, SERIAL PRIMARY KEY in SQL: INTEGER NOT NULL with a sequence default, as SQLAlchemy creates for an Integer primary key
types.str: String, VARCHAR(255). A request value longer than 255 Unicode scalars is a 422.
types.int: i32, INTEGER. A request value outside i32 is a 422.
types.float: f64, DOUBLE PRECISION. A JSON number without a fraction is accepted for a float field.
types.date: chrono::NaiveDate, DATE, ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD on the wire
types.timestamps: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL, for v3 to v5 only. The column DEFAULT is CURRENT_TIMESTAMP for v3 and v4 and now() for v5, as in the Python migration for the same version. A PATCH that supplies at least one field also sets updated_at to now().
types.optional: An optional field without a default is Option<T> and a nullable column. An optional field with a default is T in the row, NOT NULL with that column DEFAULT, and the same request default. This matches the Python migration.

fixed_routes./healthz: GET returns 200 {"status":"ok"} after SELECT 1 succeeds, else 503 {"detail":"database unavailable"}.
fixed_routes.fallback_405: A matched path with another method returns 405 {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}, except as below.
fixed_routes.v5_with_children: {parent_path}/with-children accepts only POST. GET, PATCH and DELETE on it return 422 like the Python product, whose parent id path parameter fails to parse there.

errors.404: {"detail": "not found"} for v1 to v4. v5 uses "parent not found" or "child not found".
errors.409: {"detail": "conflict"} for v1 to v4. v5 uses "relationship or unique value conflict".
errors.422: {"detail": [{"type": string, "loc": ["body" | "query" | "path", ...], "msg": string}, ...]} with at least one item.

phase2.rule: The files list above stays the phase 1 layout. A phase 2 product (contracts/rust-output-v1/phase2) has exactly the files of one shape below, chosen by the prompt alone. No shape has more than 12 files, the bundle limit, and every file keeps at most 64 blocks.

resource.applies: Every v1 to v5 prompt without a capabilities block. A prompt the phase 1 profile (tests/rust-output-v1/rust_profile.py) admits gives its phase 1 files byte for byte.
resource.cargo: reference/Cargo.toml and reference/Cargo.lock, the phase 1 crates
resource.changes: Only for a prompt the phase 1 profile refuses: src/lib.rs exports the hand-written migrator of migrations below instead of sqlx::migrate!(), and a resource may own /healthz (naming.json W2). main.rs still runs the migrator at startup and reads the phase 1 postgresql:// DATABASE_URL.

capability_postgresql.applies: A v5 prompt with capabilities or a v6 prompt, whose capabilities.database is postgresql.

capability_mongodb.applies: A v5 prompt with capabilities or a v6 prompt, whose capabilities.database is mongodb.

flow_postgresql.applies: A v7 prompt (every v7 prompt has a flow), whose capabilities.database is postgresql.

flow_mongodb.applies: A v7 prompt (every v7 prompt has a flow), whose capabilities.database is mongodb.

files.Cargo.toml: Bytes equal the reference Cargo.toml of the shape.
files.Cargo.lock: Bytes equal the reference Cargo.lock of the shape.
files.src/main.rs: Capability and flow shapes: the subcommands of phase2/services.json commands (serve, migrate upgrade, migrate downgrade, check-config); no subcommand serves. Settings are read and refused as phase2/services.json says, before any connection. serve does not migrate, as the Python product does not; it listens on SOM_APP_ADDR. A refused setting prints the Python startup message as one line on stderr and exits with status 1; an unknown subcommand exits with status 2.
files.src/lib.rs: Declares the modules of the shape. Exports pub fn router(state: AppState) -> axum::Router, AppState, the settings module of integrations, and for PostgreSQL the migrator: upgrade and downgrade of the one migration, recorded in _som_rust_migrations (naming.json W3).
files.src/models.rs: Capability shapes only: the row or document structs. The flow shapes keep them in src/schemas.rs, so a flow product fits the 12-file limit.
files.src/schemas.rs: Request and response structs as in phase 1, with naming.json R2 for every member; the flow shapes also hold the row or document structs, and the flow input and run structs.
files.src/api.rs: axum handlers and the router: the resource routes, /healthz (W2), and the auth, object, workflow, export and import routes of the prompt, with the Python statuses and bodies.
files.src/db.rs: PostgreSQL: every SQL statement as a string constant with double-quoted identifiers, run with the sqlx runtime API, and the downgrade statements. MongoDB: every collection, filter, update and index, built with bson, and the _som_counters and _som_revision documents (W6).
files.src/integrations.rs: Settings (phase2/services.json), authentication (jwt, firebase, google_oidc with its Redis session store), object storage (s3, gcs), workflows and exports, the HTTP client, and the Python-compatible JSON, number and CSV formatting they need.
files.src/flows.rs: The flow runtime: _som_flow_runs and _som_flow_leases (W6), runs, idempotency, leases, transactions, branches and undo. Flow and step names are data in a fixed table (naming.json R3); no Rust item is named by the prompt.
files.migrations/0001_<revision>.sql: PostgreSQL shapes only. The upgrade schema as in phase 1, with the first-line revision comment. The migrator records the revision in _som_rust_migrations, so a prompt table may be named _sqlx_migrations.
files.tests/api.rs: Product tests. PostgreSQL shapes read TEST_DATABASE_URL; MongoDB shapes read MONGODB_URL and SOM_TEST_DATABASE_NAME. A missing setting fails the test; it is never a skip.
files.README.md: Names the prompt package, the prompt version, the shape, the routes, every setting the product reads, and the som_app subcommands.

migrations.rule: The hand-written migrator creates _som_rust_migrations (version BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, revision TEXT NOT NULL, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()) if missing, and applies or reverts the one migration in a transaction. Schema comparison ignores _som_rust_migrations as phase 1 ignores _sqlx_migrations and the Python product's alembic_version.
